text: You know what one of my biggest fears is, like generally one of my worst fears in life is just ending up with a nonchalant man, somebody who's just there, somebody who's just so chill to the point of emotional negligence. Because honestly the type of person that I am I just cannot do that, like I feel like it would destroy my soul. I generally cannot be with somebody who is fun and expressive and obsessive at the beginning, like doing all the right things, laughing so hard at my jokes, dancing in the kitchen, being goofy, and then six months later he's just acting like all of that was a phase. Look, the way she talks makes it sound like ending up with a nonchalant man is something that just happens to her. As if men fall out of the sky, land in her living room, and she has no say in who she dates. But that's not how things work. The truth is simple, you decide who you date, and normally already after a few months you know a lot about the person. Their habits, values, mindset, emotional stability, it all shows with time. If six months later he suddenly becomes a different person, then either he's a shapeshifter or the signs were there but you ignored them. It's like when a guy says everything was perfect for a year and then she suddenly cheated. Really? Suddenly? And then when you look closer, turns out she was texting other guys, staying in contact with an ex, going out alone, disrespecting him, and he just didn't want to see any of it. People rarely change overnight. What actually happens is that we overlook red flags because we want the fantasy more than the truth. And even if, even if, someone pulls off an oscar-winning performance for six straight months and then switches their whole personality, fine, just leave. It's not the end of the world. It's not the biggest fear ever situation. It's just a breakup. You move on and you choose better next time.
